content: The salicylate levels increase when administered at moderate doses but decrease at higher doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. Calcium carbonate reduces the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH, which decreases the solubility of atazanavir. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Atazanavir should be administered 2 hours before or 1 hour after calcium carbonate. Close monitoring is recommended. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of atenolol by an unspecified mechanism, likely through inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Atenolol and calcium carbonate should be separated by 2 hours. Close monitoring is advised. Calcium carbonate reduces the levels of azithromycin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Azithromycin and calcium carbonate should be separated by 2 hours. Close monitoring is recommended. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract, reducing its absorption. Studies in monkeys have shown significantly decreased plasma levels when co-administered with calcium, aluminum, or iron. Human studies have not been conducted. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of bearberry by passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Close monitoring is recommended. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of benazepril by an unspecified mechanism. Close monitoring is advised. Bendroflumethiazide increases calcium carbonate levels by decreasing renal clearance and decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of benzphetamine by passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Close monitoring is recommended. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of betaxolol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Betaxolol and calcium carbonate should be separated by 2 hours. Close monitoring is advised. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of bictegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Bictegravir can be taken 2 hours before antacids containing aluminum, magnesium, or calcium under fasting conditions. However, bictegravir and calcium-containing supplements can be taken together with food. Routine administration of bictegravir under fasting conditions simultaneously with, or 2 hours after, calcium supplements or antacids containing calcium is not recommended. Close monitoring is advised. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of bisoprolol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Bisoprolol and calcium carbonate should be separated by 2 hours. Close monitoring is recommended. Blessed thistle theoretically decreases the effects of calcium carbonate through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of bosutinib by increasing gastric pH. Bosutinib has pH-dependent solubility. Short-acting antacids may be used if administration is separated by 2 hours. Close monitoring is recommended. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Bumetanide decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide and calcium carbonate by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of cabotegravir by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Calcium carbonate has a similar effect. Antacid products should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after oral cabotegravir. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Caffeine decreases calcium carbonate levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Calcitonin salmon increases magnesium hydroxide levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Topical calcitriol increases calcium carbonate levels through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially leading to hypercalcemia. Close monitoring is recommended. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of captopril by an unspecified mechanism, likely by reducing its absorption. Close monitoring is advised. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH and inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Conversely, carbonyl iron increases calcium carbonate levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to oral forms. The clinical significance is unknown. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of carvedilol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Carvedilol and calcium carbonate should be separated by 2 hours. Close monitoring is recommended. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of cefdinir, cefditoren, and cefpodoxime by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to oral forms. Close monitoring is recommended. Ceftriaxone and calcium carbonate are contraindicated due to the risk of potentially fatal particulate precipitation in the lungs and kidneys when calcium-containing solutions are used with intravenous ceftriaxone. Separate administration by at least 48 hours. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Close monitoring is recommended. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of celecoxib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Celecoxib and calcium carbonate should be separated by 2 hours. Close monitoring is advised. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of celiprolol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Celiprolol and calcium carbonate should be separated by 2 hours. Close monitoring is recommended. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of chenodiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Chenodiol and calcium carbonate should be separated by 2 hours. Close monitoring is recommended. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Magnesium hydroxide has a similar effect. Doses should be separated by at least 4 hours. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Chlorothiazide decreases magnesium hydroxide levels and increases calcium carbonate levels by altering renal clearance. These interactions may increase the risk of alkalosis and hypercalcemia. The clinical significance is unknown. Chlorthalidone increases calcium carbonate levels and decreases magnesium hydroxide levels by altering renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. Calcium carbonate and choline magnesium trisalicylate interact through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Salicylate levels increase at moderate doses but decrease at high doses due to enhanced renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance is unknown. Calcium carbonate decreases chromium levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Chromium and calcium carbonate should be separated by 2 hours. The clinical significance is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide decreases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Co-administration with multivalent cation-containing products may reduce ciprofloxacin bioavailability by up to 90%. Ciprofloxacin should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these products. Close monitoring is recommended. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of clevidipine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Close monitoring is advised. Conjugated estrogens decrease magnesium hydroxide levels by shifting magnesium from blood to tissue storage. The clinical significance is unknown. Cortisone decreases calcium carbonate levels by increasing elimination. The clinical significance is unknown. Magnesium hydroxide decreases crizotinib levels by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility and bioavailability. Calcium carbonate has a similar effect. No formal studies have been conducted. Close monitoring is recommended. Cyclopenthiazide decreases magnesium hydroxide levels and increases calcium carbonate levels by altering renal clearance. These interactions may increase the risk of alkalosis and hypercalcemia. The clinical significance is unknown. Calcium carbonate decreases cyclosporine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Cyclosporine and calcium carbonate should be separated by 2 hours. Close monitoring is recommended. Calcium carbonate decreases dabrafenib levels by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility and bioavailability. Drugs that alter upper gastrointestinal pH, such as proton pump inhibitors, H2 blockers, and antacids, may exacerbate this effect. Close monitoring is recommended. Calcium carbonate decreases dapsone levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Calcium carbonate decreases dasatinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Magnesium hydroxide decreases deferiprone levels by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. Calcium carbonate has a similar effect. Deferiprone may bind polyvalent cations such as iron, aluminum, and zinc. Administration should be separated by at least 4 hours. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Deferoxamine decreases calcium carbonate levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Deferoxamine chelates iron, but its affinity for other minerals is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. Magnesium hydroxide and deflazacort both decrease serum potassium levels. Deflazacort decreases calcium carbonate levels by increasing elimination. The clinical significance is unknown. Calcium carbonate decreases delafloxacin levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Oral delafloxacin chelates with alkaline earth and transition metal cations. Administration should be separated by at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Magnesium hydroxide decreases demeclocycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Calcium carbonate has a similar effect. Administration should be separated by 2 hours. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Devil's claw decreases the effects of calcium carbonate through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown. Dexamethasone decreases calcium carbonate levels by increasing elimination. The clinical significance is unknown. Calcium carbonate increases dextroamphetamine levels through passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Close monitoring is recommended.
